rationale: The workflow already implements the evidence-supported Gradle dependency cache (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) using actions/cache@v4, caching ~/.gradle/caches, ~/.gradle/wrapper, and ./.gradle/loom-cache with a key derived from runner.os and hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties'), plus restore-keys. This is equal to or more comprehensive than the experiment example, so re-adding it would be a redundant, unrelated change. The matrix contains only one job (java 21 on ubuntu-24.04), so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST would cancel nothing and provide no benefit. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks sufficient representative history: CI history is marked not_a_measured_baseline with only two runs, so a safe timeout budget cannot be derived. Other patterns (cancel-stale, change-filter, skip-workflow) are CI-service or trigger-level concerns not supported as minimal workflow changes here, and the conditional publish/upload step must be preserved unchanged. No additional evidence-supported optimization applies without speculative or unrelated modifications.
